title: device_map
description: The `device_map` content kind (megaplan 1.7, 1.11 and tasks 4-A1, 4-M1): which Minecraft block (or entity) a Night City device class becomes, and how big it is, since the DLL sends no size (Phase 0 c). One file per Cyberpunk script class, named after it in snake_case. `class` is the RTTI class name the DLL sends in `devices.cls` (at most 48 characters); `kind` is the section 1.11 device kind, and its toggle bit belongs to the kind: door 1, gate 2, light 4, camera 8, terminal 16, vending 32, traffic 64, elevator 128, turret 256, screen 512, container 1024. `block` is the block placed at the device's position; `alt_block` replaces it while `alt_when` holds (`secure`: flag bit 2, an iron door for a secure door; `readable`: the loot can be read, a chest for a container); `entity` is an entity hung on the block's front (a glow item frame that shows the map image); `size` is [width, height, depth] in blocks along the device's facing; `attachments` are extra blocks at an offset [dx, dy, dz] from the placement corner, always or only while the device is locked (the red lamp above a locked door, the lift call button); `shops` lists the `shop` ids a vending device picks from (stable per device id). Blocks are vanilla ids or the cyberblock device blocks of art/gen_block_art.py (4A). Every one of them also has the block property quest_locked (false/true) except the crate; the others are: lamp_<dye> [lit] for the 16 dyes of the neon blocks; eye_camera [facing, mode off|on|alarm|friendly]; net_port [breached, facing]; vending_machine [broken, facing]; traffic_lamp [signal off|red|amber|green]; lift_platform [moving]; lift_call_button [facing, lit]; turret [facing, mode off|active|friendly]; sliding_gate [facing, step 0..4]; screen_frame [facing, on]; crate []. A file with the same id as a default replaces it, so a datapack ships only the classes it changes.
